instrument: International Plant Protection Convention (IPPC)
description: Aims to prevent the introduction and spread of plant pests across borders while facilitating safe trade. Establishes standards for phytosanitary measures, encourages harmonization, and creates a framework for international surveillance, certification, and response.

actionTracks.rationale: Strengthens national plant health systems and surveillance, building capacity for pest detection.
Prevents international spread of pests affecting food security and ecological balance.
Establishes global standards for phytosanitary certification, supporting safe trade.
Links plant protection with broader environmental health by preventing ecosystem destabilization.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Reinforces equitable responsibilities across countries through harmonized plant health measures.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Aims to preserve ecological balance by preventing the spread of invasive plant pests.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Emphasizes prevention over reaction, promoting long-term environmental stewardship.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Facilitates cross-sectoral and intergovernmental collaboration through regional organizations.

governanceRole: Legally binding framework for coordinated global plant health governance; harmonized international standards and surveillance systems; integrates plant health with trade, food security, and environmental protection.
limitations: No binding obligations on environmental monitoring or climate-related plant risks. Collaboration with other One Health instruments is not formally structured.
provisions: Preamble: Takes into account principles governing protection of plant, human, animal health, and environment. Article VIII(1): Cooperation on pest information exchange. Article XX: Provision of technical assistance.
interlinkages: WTO Agreement on Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures (SPS)

instrument: International Convention for Protection of New Plant Varieties (UPOV)
description: Provides an effective system of plant variety protection to encourage development of new varieties, granting breeders exclusive rights.

actionTracks.rationale: Improved plant varieties contribute to higher yield and nutrition for a stable food chain.
Encourages varieties that are climate-smart and adaptive to climate change.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Provides benefits to breeders and farmers alike.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Supports crop innovation for environmental challenges.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Ensures future food security and sustainability.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Interdisciplinary collaboration between science, agri-business, and farmers.

governanceRole: Allows use of protected varieties for breeding new varieties (Breeder's Exemption). Supports climate change adaptation and capacity building for agricultural productivity.
limitations: Implementation challenges regarding testing requirements for low-resource countries. Strong breeders' rights may influence access for farmers or researchers.
provisions: Article 15(1)(iii): Breeders' Exemption. Article 15(2): Farmer's Privilege to save/reuse seeds. Article 17: Public Interest Exception.
interlinkages: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), Nagoya Protocol

instrument: Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat (Ramsar Convention)
description: Establishes a global framework for wise use and conservation of wetlands. Parties must designate sites, maintain ecological character, and monitor changes.

actionTracks.rationale: Builds cross-sector capacity for ecosystem-public health collaboration.
Addresses ecological balance and biodiversity, mitigating zoonotic/pollution risks.
Reduces food-water-safety risks through wetland protection.
Integrates environment into One Health by conserving ecosystems vital for health resilience.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes equity by conserving wetlands vital to human-animal-environment alike.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Supports biodiversity and socio-ecological equilibrium.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Encourages stewardship and sustainable use of shared ecosystems.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Encourages multisectoral governance via national focal points, COP bodies, and public participation.

governanceRole: Mandated ecological monitoring and reporting. Infrastructure for cooperation via COP and STRP. Wise-use principle offering flexible implementation.
limitations: Broad obligations without binding enforcement mechanisms. Variation in implementation of 'wise use'. Limited explicit reference to human health.
provisions: Article 1: Defines wetlands broadly. Article 2: Designate Ramsar sites. Article 3: Plan for conservation/wise use. Article 8: International cooperation.

instrument: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES)
description: Regulates international trade in wildlife to ensure survival of vulnerable species via Appendices and permitting systems.

actionTracks.rationale: States that the Convention should not alter domestic measures pertaining to public health or veterinary quarantine.
Focuses on the protection of wild flora and fauna as part of the environment.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Shared wildlife heritage.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Prevents biodiversity loss.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Humans as stewards of wildlife.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: International cooperation for enforcement.

governanceRole: Reduces risk of zoonotic disease emergence via reporting on pathogen spillover in trade. Collaborates with WOAH. Permitting system regulates human-animal contact points.
limitations: Limited scope focused on trade rather than broad ecosystem health. Relies on national resource availability for implementation.
provisions: Article III(2)(c) & VIII(3): Safe transport of live specimens to minimize injury or damage to health. Article III(3)(b): Suitable housing requirements.

instrument: Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species of Wild Animals (Bonn Convention; CMS)
description: Provides framework to restore or maintain favorable conservation status of migratory species by protecting habitats, regulating use, and fostering regional agreements.

actionTracks.rationale: Integrates environment in One Health by promoting ecosystem conservation, land management, and connectivity for population health.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Protects species and habitats across all Parties for equitable ecosystem benefit.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Promotes socio-ecological balance by conserving migratory habitats and connectivity.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Emphasizes stewardship via habitat restoration and species protection.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Advances transdisciplinarity through COP, Scientific Council, and agreements involving health/environment sectors.

governanceRole: Multisectoral surveillance and rapid risk response for wildlife health. Framework for cooperation via MoUs. Global data-sharing platforms.
limitations: Fragmented adoption of regional agreements. Enforcement gaps due to varying national capacities. Public health referenced only indirectly.
provisions: Art. 2: Obliges protection of species. Art. 3: Prohibits specified take/trade. COP Resolutions address wildlife health, zoonoses, and biosecurity.

instrument: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)
description: Comprehensive legal framework governing all uses of the world's oceans, establishing state rights/duties, and regulating marine environmental protection and resources.

actionTracks.rationale: Builds institutional capacity for marine monitoring and pollution response.
Addresses risks from marine pollution that drive disease emergence at the human-animal-ocean interface.
Regulates living marine resources with direct implications for aquatic food safety.
Integrates the marine environment through binding obligations on pollution prevention.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Affirms equitable sharing of ocean resources and special requirements of developing states.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Requires conservation to maintain populations and protect fragile ecosystems.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Imposes a binding duty to protect and preserve the marine environment.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Mandates global and regional cooperation for environmental standards.

governanceRole: Binding legal framework for marine environmental protection. Mandatory monitoring and transboundary notification. Conservation of aquatic resources.
limitations: Limited direct integration with human/animal health systems. Enforcement relies heavily on flag state compliance.
provisions: Article 192: Obligation to protect marine environment. Article 194(5): Protect rare ecosystems. Article 196: Prevent introduction of alien species.
interlinkages: Aquatic Animal Health Code, CBD, GBF, Ramsar

instrument: Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal
description: Aims to control transboundary movement and management of hazardous wastes. Regulates export/import, prevents illegal dumping, and promotes waste risk reduction.

actionTracks.rationale: Builds national capacity for waste management and surveillance systems.
Advances safeguards against pollution and ecosystem degradation from hazardous waste.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Helps low-income countries prevent illegal dumping and environmental injustice.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Reduces toxic exposures that disrupt ecosystems, biodiversity, and food systems.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Embodies stewardship through waste minimization and safe disposal.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Fosters multisectoral engagement through obligations on monitoring and reporting.

governanceRole: Reduces shared health risks from waste pollution. Supports national system strengthening for waste governance. Promotes international cooperation.
limitations: Focus primarily on waste management rather than broader health pathways. Variation in enforcement across contexts.
provisions: Article 4: Prohibits export/import of hazardous waste without informed consent. Article 5: Designate national authorities. Article 10: Technical assistance.

instrument: Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)
description: Provides an overarching framework on biodiversity targeting conservation, sustainable use, and fair/equitable sharing of genetic resources.

actionTracks.rationale: Pathogen sharing facilitates disease prevention and control.
Includes pathogens as genetic resources to assist with controlling zoonotic diseases.
Emphasizes importance of biodiversity as an integral pillar of the environment.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes fair benefit sharing.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Acknowledges Indigenous knowledge.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Emphasizes biodiversity balance.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Encourages sustainable use for the future.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Supports multisector programs.

governanceRole: Adopted Global One Health Policy for pandemic prevention. WHO-CBD collaboration on monitoring. Risk management tools and equity focus.
limitations: Many health components remain voluntary. Lack of binding provisions to harmonize multi-sector legislation. Monitoring indicators still in development.
provisions: Article 8: In-situ conservation and managing LMO risks. Article 14: Environmental impact assessments. Article 15: Access to genetic resources.
interlinkages: Mother Convention of Cartagena and Nagoya Protocols

instrument: Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety (Cartagena Protocol)
description: Protocol to the CBD ensuring safe transport, handling, and use of living modified organisms (LMOs) that may adversely affect biodiversity and human health.

actionTracks.rationale: LMOs are agricultural and implicate food safety.
Aims to minimize biotechnology risks to the environment and human health.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Capacity building for developing countries.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Public participation in country.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Protects biodiversity and health.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Precautionary responsibility.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: International scientific cooperation.

governanceRole: Risk assessment guidance for LMOs. Biosafety Clearing-House for information sharing. Health-related indicators in reporting.
limitations: Primary emphasis on environmental impacts may not fully encompass human/animal health. Risk guidelines are non-binding. Resource constraints.
provisions: Article 1: Precautionary approach. Article 15: Risk assessment considering biodiversity and human health. Article 16: Risk management.
interlinkages: Codex Principles for Foods Derived from Modern Biotechnology

instrument: Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and the Fair and Equitable Sharing of Benefits Arising from their Utilization
description: Protocol to the CBD providing a transparent legal framework for fair and equitable benefit-sharing arising from the utilization of genetic resources.

actionTracks.rationale: Ensures pathogens are shared to limit risks to epidemics.
Facilitates sharing of resources relevant to combating diseases.
Genetic resource sharing improves biodiversity as an aspect of the environment.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Fair and equitable sharing of benefits from genetic resources.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Addresses rights of indigenous/local communities, ensuring prior informed consent.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Encourages collaboration across research, public health, and industry.

governanceRole: Framework for equitable benefit-sharing supporting health equity. ABS Clearing-House for info exchange. Capacity building for developing countries.
limitations: Varied national implementation of ABS legislation. Complex administrative processes for authorization. Legal uncertainty regarding scope interpretation.
provisions: Article 8(b): Expeditious access to resources for health emergencies. Article 9: Benefits toward conservation. Article 12: Traditional knowledge benefit-sharing.

instrument: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
description: Framework for intergovernmental efforts to tackle climate change, committing Parties to limit emissions and develop responses protecting vulnerable populations.

actionTracks.rationale: Frames climate change as causing adverse effects and obligates prevention.
Requires adaptation measures to reduce vulnerability to health impacts like disease.
Built on protecting the climate system in light of environmental commitments.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Frames climate change as cross-sectoral requiring broad coordination.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Common but differentiated responsibilities explicitly recognizes inequality.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Recognizes adverse effects on ecosystems and links environmental stability to well-being.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Calls to protect climate system for present and future generations.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Calls for scientific cooperation, information exchange, and coordination.

governanceRole: Established a Health Programme (COP26). Multisectoral agricultural initiatives. Operationalized Loss and Damage Fund. Emphasizes climate-health knowledge sharing.
limitations: Slow progress on mitigation. Finance gaps. Health is not a central component of core climate negotiations. Varied national reporting.
provisions: Article 1: Defines adverse effects including human health. Article 2: Objective to stabilize GHG levels. Article 4.1: Adaptation planning and minimizing impacts.
interlinkages: WHO Pandemic Agreement, Paris Agreement, UNCCD

instrument: Paris Agreement
description: Agreement under UNFCCC aiming to limit global temperature rise via nationally determined contributions (NDCs).

actionTracks.rationale: Temperature reduction goals will slow the spread of vectors.
Goals are an effort to protect the environment and humans.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Just transitions and financing for the poor.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Indigenous and human rights.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Limits warming for ecosystems.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Intergenerational equity.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: All nations meant to contribute.

governanceRole: Encourages inclusive adaptation planning (Article 7.9). Glasgow Climate Pact emphasizes integrated health-climate approaches. Enhances capacity building and knowledge sharing.
limitations: Limited explicit health focus. Implementation relies on voluntary NDC fulfillment. Resource constraints for climate-related health measures.
provisions: Article 7: Enhancing adaptive capacity to protect people/ecosystems via participatory approaches. Article 8: Building resilience regarding loss and damage.

instrument: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD)
description: Legally binding agreement focused on land degradation and desertification. Promotes sustainable land management, ecosystem restoration, and climate resilience.

actionTracks.rationale: Supports national capacity-building for sustainable land management.
Addresses ecological shifts that create favorable conditions for zoonotic spillover.
Promotes actions to reduce vulnerability to endemic/vector-borne diseases in arid regions.
Centers environmental integrity by reversing land degradation.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Prioritizes rural/dryland communities facing degradation and health vulnerability.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Advances balance through land restoration and biodiversity conservation.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Supports long-term intergenerational responsibility for land/water.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Fosters collaboration between agriculture, climate, health, and indigenous knowledge.

governanceRole: Recognizes biodiversity loss links to spillover/malnutrition. Promotes integrated land management balancing ecosystems and livelihoods. Strengthens funding mechanisms.
limitations: Health impacts are implied but not explicitly embedded in operational provisions. Implementation gaps due to limited national resources.
provisions: Article 2: Mitigating drought as a global priority. Article 10: National Action Programmes for integrated land management. Article 16: Science and traditional knowledge.

instrument: WTO Agreement on Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures (SPS)
description: Sets rules for food safety and animal/plant health standards in international trade. Allows science-based standards while preventing arbitrary barriers.

actionTracks.rationale: Emphasizes science-based health protection measures and capacity.
Permits emergency measures to prevent cross-border outbreaks from imports.
Aims to enact measures against zoonoses risk in trade.
Enacts measures against foodborne risk in trade.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes scientific fairness in trade.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Prevents spread of pests/disease for animal and human health.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Responsibility to protect health as a dimension of well-being.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Veterinary, plant, and health sectors must collaborate.

governanceRole: Science-based approach (Article 2.2). Harmonization utilizing international standards. Capacity building for developing nations. Transparency in measures.
limitations: Harmonization across diverse contexts is complex. Some countries face ongoing resource constraints for SPS implementation.
provisions: Annex A: SPS measures cover risks from animal/plant diseases. Article 3: Harmonization with Codex/WOAH/IPPC. Article 5: Precautionary provisional measures allowed.

instrument: Rotterdam Convention on the Prior Informed Consent Procedure
description: Promotes shared responsibility in trade of hazardous chemicals. Establishes Prior Informed Consent procedure for exports, enhancing transparency and reducing health/environmental risks.

actionTracks.rationale: Enhances institutional capacities in chemical risk management for low-resource countries.
Reduces indirect drivers of disease by limiting toxicant exposure.
Requires consent to import hazardous pesticides that may contaminate food/feed.
Integrates protection into global trade by regulating cross-border chemical flows.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Enables importing countries to make informed decisions over hazardous imports.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Reduces flow of pesticides/pollutants that destabilize ecosystems.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Advances precautionary management and transparent risk sharing.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Fosters collaboration between agriculture, health, trade, and environment.

governanceRole: Empowers countries to prevent harmful chemical exposures across species. Builds multisectoral chemical governance capacity. Mandates science-based decision-making.
limitations: Health sector leadership varies. Listing processes involve multiple steps and time. Non-compliance challenges due to differing national capacities.
provisions: Article 5: Process for listing banned chemicals. Article 10: Import decisions transparently communicated. Article 14: Mandates information exchange among parties.

instrument: Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs)
description: Protects human health and the environment from bioaccumulating, persistent chemicals. Aims to eliminate/restrict POPs linked to cancer, immune disruption, etc.

actionTracks.rationale: Strengthens monitoring and regulatory oversight for health risk assessment.
Mitigates degradation that increases vulnerability to zoonoses.
Reduces foodborne/feed exposure by phasing out POPs.
Directly integrates environmental protection via legally binding controls on POPs.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Requires international cooperation to support low/middle-income countries.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Aims to restore equilibrium by eliminating disruptive toxic substances.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Embodies stewardship via lifecycle approaches to chemical use.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Reinforces transdisciplinary collaboration across sectors.

governanceRole: Links ecosystem health to human/animal health through binding controls. Strengthens national capacity for chemical risk governance. Drives international cooperation.
limitations: Sectoral focus limits explicit One Health integration. Differences in national monitoring and regulatory systems. Cross-sector coordination mechanisms lack definition.
provisions: Article 3: Bans/restricts highly toxic chemicals. Article 5: Targets unintentional POPs releases from combustion. Article 11: Promotes collaborative research/monitoring.

instrument: International Health Regulations
description: Framework for international management of public health risks and emergencies. Requires reporting of significant events and capacity building.

actionTracks.rationale: Mandates development of minimum core capacities in surveillance/response.
Governs public health emergencies resulting in epidemics/pandemics.
Includes food safety events within its scope.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Helping weaker health systems.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Non-discrimination in control measures.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Shared responsibility to prevent and control public health risks.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Requires whole-of-government approach.

governanceRole: Enhanced early warning system. Mandates One Health multisectoral collaboration. Capacity building for developing nations. States Parties Committee supports compliance.
limitations: Resource constraints in meeting core capacities. Sovereignty considerations may lead to varied implementation during emergencies.
provisions: Article 2: Prevent/control disease spread without unnecessary trade interference. Article 6: 24-hour notification for PHEIC. Article 14: Collaboration with FAO/WOAH.

instrument: Minamata Convention on Mercury
description: Global treaty to protect human health and environment from anthropogenic emissions of mercury, including lifecycle measures.

actionTracks.rationale: Strengthens health/environmental systems through monitoring and phasing out devices.
Mitigates immune harm that heightens susceptibility to infectious disease.
Addresses mercury contamination in the food chain (fish).
Regulates mercury releases into air, soil, and water.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes equity by helping countries implement safe mercury alternatives.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Seeks equilibrium by reducing contamination of aquatic systems and food webs.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Requires parties to eliminate unnecessary mercury use and emissions.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Fosters cooperation among environmental, health, and industrial sectors.

governanceRole: Limits cross-species neurotoxic exposure. Mandates national implementation plans linking environmental and health authorities. Supports technology transfer.
limitations: Informal sectors (artisanal gold mining) are hard to regulate. Phasing out timelines vary based on national capacity.
provisions: Article 4: Phases out mercury-added products. Article 7: Targets ASGM mercury use. Article 16: Encourages strategies to protect vulnerable populations.

instrument: WHO Pandemic Agreement
description: Comprehensive global framework for pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response with equity as a core principle. Explicitly integrates a One Health approach (Article 5).

actionTracks.rationale: Enhances capacities of national health systems through primary health care and infrastructure.
Requires a One Health approach, integrated surveillance, and cross-sectoral collaboration.
Requires surveillance of resistant pathogens and integration of AMR into plans.
Mandates policies that consider climate, ecosystems, and environmental drivers.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Advances equity by ensuring support for developing countries and access to countermeasures.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Strengthens inclusion of communities and Indigenous Peoples in decision-making.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Promotes socio-ecological balance by addressing environmental/human drivers of disease.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Embodies stewardship through collaborative prevention protecting ecosystems.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Establishes multisectoral collaboration across health, veterinary, and environment.

governanceRole: Prioritizes equity (Arts 2, 17, 18). Mandates One Health integration (Art 5). Creates pathogen access/benefit-sharing systems. Establishes COP.
limitations: Sovereignty clauses may influence coordinated global implementation. Resource dependence. Annex timing delays details. Non-binding implementation mechanism.
provisions: Article 4: Pandemic surveillance. Article 5: One Health approach. Article 12: Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing System. Article 18: Sustainable financing.

instrument: Terrestrial Animal Health Code
description: International standards for disease prevention, zoonoses, and AMR control. Recognized reference standard under the WTO SPS Agreement.

actionTracks.rationale: Improves veterinary infrastructure and public health preparedness.
Establishes monitoring and response mechanisms to control disease outbreaks.
Prevents and manages zoonotic diseases in terrestrial animals.
Regulates trade/disease control in livestock and animal products for food consumption.
Seeks to control antimicrobial resistance in animals.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes collaboration between veterinary, public health, and environmental sectors.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Establishes guidelines accounting for the interconnectedness of animal, human, and environment.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Encourages responsible animal health management.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Aligns veterinary, trade, and public health policies for a holistic approach.

governanceRole: Comprehensive global standards. Supports cross-sectoral collaboration. Facilitates trade while ensuring health protection. Enhances surveillance/reporting.
limitations: Limited integration with environmental governance. Low-income countries struggle with recommended infrastructure capacities.
provisions: Chapter 1.1: Notification of animal diseases. Chapter 6.2: Role of veterinary services in food safety. Chapter 6.10: Prudent use of antimicrobials.

instrument: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development
description: Establishes 27 principles for sustainable development, affirming sovereign rights alongside responsibility to prevent transboundary environmental harm.

actionTracks.rationale: Principle 9 calls for cooperation to strengthen capacity-building through scientific exchange.
Frames environmental protection as interlinked with development, promotes ecosystem integrity, and emphasizes precaution.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Affirms common but differentiated responsibilities and priority for developing countries.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Recognizes the role of women, youth, Indigenous peoples, and local communities.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Frames sustainable development as requiring harmony between humans and nature.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Calls to reduce unsustainable patterns and act as Earth stewards.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Promotes international cooperation and cross-sectoral collaboration.

governanceRole: Normative foundation for environment-health integration. Provides equity framework for One Health governance. Establishes transboundary notification obligations.
limitations: Non-binding and declaratory. Limited direct health framing; depends on interpretation through subsequent instruments.
provisions: Principle 1: Entitlement to a healthy/productive life. Principle 4: Environmental protection integral to development. Principle 15: Precautionary approach.

instrument: Aquatic Animal Health Code
description: International standards supporting the health of aquatic animals and disease control in aquatic trade.

actionTracks.rationale: Sets global standards for aquatic animal health.
Establishes guidelines for preventing and controlling aquatic zoonoses.
Regulates trade and food safety for aquatic animal products.
Promotes responsible antimicrobial use in aquaculture to prevent resistance.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Integrates fishery, aquaculture, and veterinary expertise.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Promotes biodiversity-conscious disease management.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Supports responsible aquaculture to prevent disease spillover and AMR.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Strengthens coordination between public health, fisheries, and environmental agencies.

governanceRole: Provides standards for aquatic disease control. Supports a One Health approach recognizing links to food/human health. Encourages sustainable biosecurity.
limitations: Gaps in environmental regulation integration. Challenges for small-scale/informal aquaculture in meeting standards.
provisions: Chapter 1.4: Aquatic animal health surveillance. Chapter 6.1: Recommendations for controlling AMR. Chapter 4.4: Disinfection protocols.

instrument: The International Code of Conduct on Pesticide Management
description: Voluntary framework for entities managing pesticides throughout their lifecycle. Promotes Integrated Pest Management and targets vulnerable groups' protection.

actionTracks.rationale: Calls on governments to build capacity and infrastructure for pesticide management.
Promotes practices that minimize health and environmental risks.
Addresses integrated vector management for disease control and health surveillance.
Calls for pesticide use in accordance with GAP and Codex residue limits.
Promotes biodiversity protection and minimizes adverse effects on the environment.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes equitable access to safe pesticide management for developing countries.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Identifies vulnerable groups and calls for legislative protection.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Calls for biodiversity protection and IPM/IVM to reduce agroecosystem disruption.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Embeds stewardship via a lifecycle approach and manufacturer responsibility.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Calls for coordinated action across governments, industry, academia, and civil society.

Recognizes environmental drivers of AMR calling for surveillance.
Positions pollution and degradation as central to health inequality.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes equity via support for developing countries.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Recognizes structural threats to health/ecosystems.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Emphasizes prevention and life-cycle approaches.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Embeds transdisciplinary action across diverse sectors.

governanceRole: Operationalizes OH across clusters. Expands evidence base with WHO/FAO/WOAH. Promotes multisectoral coordination platforms.
limitations: No formal intersectoral mandates. Limited compliance tracking. Funding constraints for LMICs.
provisions: OP 24: OH approach across domains. OP 25-27: Biodiversity-health integration. OP 29-35: OH-based AMR governance.
interlinkages: CBD, GBF, GAP for Biodiversity and Health

instrument: Conference Resolution 6/2019: Antimicrobial Resistance
description: Reaffirms FAO's AMR leadership, endorsing Quadripartite collaboration, urging surveillance/prudent use, and supporting LMICs.

actionTracks.rationale: Calls for cross-sectoral capacity building.
Promotes early detection of threats.
Links AMR to safety and urges prudent use.
Reinforces stewardship to curb resistance.
Expands focus to environmental AMR drivers.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes shared responsibilities across domains.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Recognizes environmental contamination as AMR driver.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Emphasizes responsible use and sustainable practices.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Strengthens joint AMR governance through Quadripartite.

governanceRole: Endorses expanded Tripartite/UNEP framework. Aligns with WHO GAP. Prioritizes support for LMICs.
limitations: Lacks clarity on operationalizing environmental surveillance. No structured roles for civil society.
provisions: OP 1: Supports Tripartite work. OP 4: Establish coordination for WHO GAP. OP 7: Support for developing countries.
interlinkages: WHO GAP on AMR, WOAH Strategy on AMR

instrument: Resolution 14: OIE's Engagement in the One Health Global Effort to Control Antimicrobial Resistance
description: Strengthens global coordination for AMR via OH approach, focusing on action plans, Tripartite coordination, and sustainable investments.

actionTracks.rationale: Supports veterinary capacities and AMR surveillance.
Recognizes AMR as a transboundary threat.
Addresses use in food-producing animals.
Focuses on reducing misuse supporting stewardship.
Highlights environmental contamination from waste.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes veterinary roles in multisectoral efforts.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Recognizes AMR as threat to balance.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Calls for behavioral change in agricultural practices.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Coordinates global cross-sector monitoring efforts.

governanceRole: Promotes antimicrobial stewardship. Supports ANIMUSE database for harmonized surveillance. Capacity building in veterinary governance.
limitations: Limited regulation of antimicrobials in animal sectors. Inconsistent reporting. Insufficient enforcement capacity in some countries.
provisions: Para 3: Reaffirms commitment to NAPs. Para 4: ANIMUSE reporting. Para 9: Urges contributions to Partner Fund for LMICs.
interlinkages: WHO GAP on AMR, WOAH Strategy on AMR, Codex CXC 61-2005

instrument: WHA 73.5: Strengthening efforts on food safety
description: Reaffirms food safety as core to health. Calls for OH approach integrating health, agriculture, trade, and environment policies.

actionTracks.rationale: Encourages health-in-all-policies for food safety.
Promotes actions across supply chain for safety.
Promotes coherent actions to tackle foodborne AMR.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Integrates food safety into national multi-sector policies.

principles.name: Sociopolitical and multicultural parity (equal rights/opportunities) and inclusion/engagement of marginalized voices
principles.narrative: Advocates for sustainability and access for all.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Promotes responsible investment in safety systems.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Emphasizes coordinated global governance.

governanceRole: Promotes OH cross-sector collaboration. Calls for health-in-all-policies. Advocates for Codex usage and WHO/FAO collaboration.
limitations: Focus remains largely on national governments with less explicit integration of communities. Implementation varies by capacity.
provisions: Preamble: OH approach includes managing risks along food chain. OP 1(3): Urges cross-sector collaboration and sustainability.
interlinkages: Codex CXS 193-1995, Codex CXC 1-1969, WTO SPS

instrument: WHA 74.7: Strengthening WHO preparedness for and response to health emergencies
description: Roadmap for strengthening emergency capacities. Calls for OH collaboration, improved surveillance, and equitable access to tools.

actionTracks.rationale: Reinforces capacity building under the IHR.
Emphasizes early detection and response through OH approach.
Promotes AMR prevention during emergencies.
Supports collaboration among WHO/FAO/WOAH/UNEP.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Emphasizes collaborative preparedness across domains.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Links emergencies to environmental disruption.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Calls for proactive stewardship and long-term resilience.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Advances formal collaboration among Quadripartite agencies.

governanceRole: Institutionalizes OH coordination globally. Integrates surveillance (GLEWS). Supports country-led multisectoral preparedness.
limitations: Human health remains dominant frame. Operational specificity lacking. Member State focus may sideline non-state expertise.
provisions: OP 7(3): All-hazard OH approach. OP 8-10: Reform GLEWS, establish common strategy on OH with partners.
interlinkages: IHR, WHO Pandemic Agreement, PIP Framework

instrument: UNEA Resolultion 5/6: Biodiversity and Health
description: Recognizes interlinkages between biodiversity and well-being. Emphasizes OH in preventing pandemics and supports cross-policy integration.

actionTracks.rationale: Strengthens OH coordination and data systems.
Calls to reduce spillover risks.
Encourages restoration buffering against diseases.
Embeds conservation into health governance.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Support for developing countries in OH implementation.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Re-centers ecosystem services as foundational to health.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Supports intergenerational stewardship.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Calls for transdisciplinary approaches.

governanceRole: Promotes capacity building in LMICs. Aligns biodiversity with zoonotic prevention. Highlights risks during spillover events.
limitations: Health sector engagement is advisory. Lacks measurable benchmarks for integration progress.
provisions: OP 2: Mainstream biodiversity-health linkages. OP 5: Reduce spillover via sustainable use. OP 13: Highlights AMR priority.

instrument: WHA 75.13: Global strategy on infection prevention and control
description: Mandates development of global strategy on IPC to reduce healthcare infections and AMR, aligning with WASH and OH frameworks.

actionTracks.rationale: Strengthens IPC capacities across all levels of care.
Recognizes IPC as cornerstone of outbreak response.
Integrates IPC with food safety and WASH systems.
Directly links IPC to curbing AMR.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Calls for IPC measures across all settings.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Recognizes interplay of health, WASH, and environment.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Advocates science-based IPC preventing harm.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Aligns IPC with AMR, safety, and environmental programs.

governanceRole: Integrates IPC with AMR/WASH. Emphasizes workforce development. Establishes measurable implementation frameworks.
limitations: Weak IPC presence outside hospitals disrupts coordination. Fragmented HAI data. IPC professionals lack structural authority.
provisions: OP3: Ensure functional IPC programmes taking into account OH approach. OP6: Ensure sustainable IPC/WASH infrastructures. OP2: Translate strategy into action plan.

instrument: WHA 76.17: The impact of chemicals, waste and pollution on human health
description: Calls for commitments to the WHO Global Strategy to address risks of plastics, chemicals, and waste via cross-sector engagement.

actionTracks.rationale: Strengthens surveillance capacities for impacts of pollution.
Calls for regulation of pollutants in food systems.
Centers pollution as key determinant in health strategies.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Acknowledges harmful effects of pollution on ecosystems.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Promotes policies reducing pollution sustainably.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Encourages cooperation among health and environment authorities.

governanceRole: Strengthens biomonitoring systems. Institutionalizes multisector governance via Global Framework on Chemicals. Aligns pollution policy with health goals.
limitations: Fragmented governance across sectors. Weak national biomonitoring systems. Limited health sector engagement in pollution policy.
provisions: Para 1: Take impact of chemicals into account. Para 4: Requests OH research linkages regarding pollution/waste.

instrument: CMS Resolution 12.6: Wildlife health & migratory species
description: Affirms interdependence of wildlife, human, and ecosystem health. Emphasizes OH-based governance and non-lethal responses.

actionTracks.rationale: Promotes national capacity building and integration of wildlife health.
Acknowledges migratory wildlife role in disease emergence.
Emphasizes cumulative pressures on species.
Links ecosystem degradation to declining resilience.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Encourages support to low-income countries.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Defines healthy ecosystems as determinants of resilience.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Emphasizes ecosystem-based prevention and non-lethal response.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Strengthens cross-border collaboration among agencies.

governanceRole: Recognizes environmental drivers of disease. Advocates upstream non-lethal management. Consolidates previous resolutions.
limitations: No formal compliance framework. Health sector roles are supportive rather than institutionalized. Data limitations in Global South.
provisions: Preamble: Recognizes full suite of drivers. Para 4: Non-lethal science-based responses. Para 5: Links wildlife health to OH goals.

instrument: CMS Resolution 14/18: Avian influenza
description: Addresses HPAI threat to birds, ecosystems, and humans via OH approach. Rejects culling/habitat destruction.

actionTracks.rationale: Calls for wildlife contingency planning and preparedness.
Prioritizes mitigation of transmission across interfaces.
Seeks to conserve vulnerable bird populations.
Promotes ecosystem integrity opposing habitat degradation.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Recognizes inequities and calls for global support.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Frames intact ecosystems as buffers against emergence.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Opposes destructive responses calling for biosecurity.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Institutionalizes cross-border coordination.

governanceRole: Formally applies OH lens to HPAI outbreak response. Rejects harmful wildlife control. Establishes conservation-driven surveillance.
limitations: Implementation is voluntary. Human health agencies are not mandated implementers. Limited guidance on integrating surveillance.
provisions: Para 1: National HPAI contingency plans. Para 2: Avoids culling. Para 3: Multisectoral spillover measures. Para 4: Surveillance and data-sharing.
interlinkages: CMS, Ramsar, IHR, PIP Framework, Terrestrial Animal Health Code

instrument: Resolution Conf. 10.21 (Rev. CoP19): Transport of live specimens
description: Guidelines for humane, health-conscious transport of CITES-listed species, adopting IATA standards to minimize stress and disease transmission.

actionTracks.rationale: Encourages capacity for health-sensitive wildlife transport.
Addresses disease transmission linked to transport stress.
Reduces morbidity exacerbating pressures on ecosystems.

principles.name: Equity between sectors and disciplines
principles.narrative: Promotes safety in trade via standardized protocols.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Advances stewardship by minimizing transport cruelty/harm.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Encourages coordination between CITES, IATA, WOAH.

governanceRole: Codifies health safeguards in logistics. Recognizes disease risks linked to handling. Encourages expert collaboration.
limitations: Focus on conservation over integrated disease surveillance. Relies on national legislation. Voluntary adoption lacks accountability.
provisions: Preamble Para 8: Stress increases disease risk. Rec 2: Use IATA standards. Rec 3(d): Investigate high-mortality shipments.

instrument: Resolution Conf. 13.10 (Rev. CoP14): Trade in invasive alien species
description: Acknowledges trade in live animals/plants contributes to IAS spread. Recommends incorporating IAS risks into permitting and CBD collaboration.

actionTracks.rationale: Recognizes IAS facilitate zoonotic emergence.
Highlights health impacts on ecosystems and endemic species.
Emphasizes integrated regulation preventing biological invasions.

principles.name: Socio-ecological equilibrium
principles.narrative: Accounts for ecosystem vulnerability in live trade.

principles.name: Stewardship
principles.narrative: Calls for precaution in trade affecting shared ecosystems.

principles.name: Transdisciplinarity and multisectoral collaboration
principles.narrative: Promotes inter-convention cooperation (CITES-CBD).

governanceRole: Integrates IAS prevention into trade governance. Promotes risk consultation between states. Strengthens CITES/CBD cooperation.
limitations: No explicit integration of public health/veterinary sectors. Relies on national capacity to regulate risk.
provisions: Rec 1(a): Consider IAS risks in legislation. Rec 1(b): Exporters consult importers. Rec 1(c): Synergy between CITES and CBD.
